requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST use
the current workspace source at book-render time and explicitly identify its
contents as current workspace source notes.
rationale:
The subject has two obligations. The notes view must use the current workspace source at book-render time. It must also explicitly identify its contents as current workspace source notes.

`src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[each_render_reads_current_notes_and_keeps_recorded_reviews_without_writing]` is marked `{test}` for the subject and covers both.

- **Current source at render time:**
  - The test renders once, using the `render` helper, which calls `pages`.
  - It then rewrites `code.rs`, changing "Original platform" to "Updated platform", and renders again.
  - It asserts that the second render contains "Updated platform explanation.".
  - It asserts that the part of the second render before "Review:" does not contain "Original platform explanation.".
  - Together these rule out a stale or cached read. The re-render also leaves the saved review in place, which shows the notes come from the source and not from a stored copy.
- **Explicit identification:** The test asserts that the content contains "Current workspace source notes". The `pages` function in `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs` emits this text as a bold label, "**Current workspace source notes**, read at book-render time". The assertion therefore checks the required label.

The remaining assertions in that test (recorded review preserved, no writes, no `target` directory) belong to `render_only`, a separate requirement. Neither the cited parent `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` nor any other cited requirement adds obligations that need extra tests here.

I found no gap.
